title: Audit of prehospital thrombolysis by general practitioners in peripheral practices in Grampian.
finding: 146 (35%) of 414 thrombolytic administrations given by GPs and 268 (65%) deferred to hospital; standard readily achieved when GPs gave treatment, not otherwise.
change: Periodic feedback of audit findings to GPs with practice case reviews.

detail.setting: General practices at least 30 minutes from Aberdeen Royal Infirmary, Grampian

cycle1.result: 146 (35%) of 414 thrombolytic administrations given by GPs and 268 (65%) deferred to hospital; standard readily achieved when GPs gave treatment, not otherwise.

detail.intervention: Periodic feedback of audit findings to GPs with practice case reviews.
detail.other_findings: Knowledge of benefits and feedback did not increase prehospital thrombolysis use.
detail.citation: Rawles J, Sinclair C, Jennings K, Ritchie L, Waugh N. Audit of prehospital thrombolysis by general practitioners in peripheral practices in Grampian. Heart. 1998;80(3):231-234. doi:10.1136/hrt.80.3.231. PMID: 9875080.

paper.citation: Rawles J, Sinclair C, Jennings K, Ritchie L, Waugh N. Audit of prehospital thrombolysis by general practitioners in peripheral practices in Grampian. Heart. 1998;80(3):231-234. doi:10.1136/hrt.80.3.231. PMID: 9875080.
paper.title: Audit of prehospital thrombolysis by general practitioners in peripheral practices in Grampian.

title: Sequential audits of geriatric care: measuring change in structure and process and the contribution of clinical audit.
topic: Geriatric long-term and day hospital care standards
standard: Royal College of Physicians CARE scheme (long-term care) and RCP geriatric day hospital audit scheme

detail.setting: 17 nursing homes and geriatric long-stay wards; 27 geriatric day hospitals

cycle2.period: Eight months (long-term care) and six months (day hospitals) after cycle 1
cycle2.result: Improvement outweighed deterioration in all domains of geriatric care.

detail.other_findings: Paper mainly describes methods for analysing sequential audits.
detail.citation: Brocklehurst J, Dickinson E, Windsor J. Sequential audits of geriatric care: measuring change in structure and process and the contribution of clinical audit. J R Coll Physicians Lond. 1998;32(6):564-567. doi:10.1016/s0035-8819(25)01805-7. PMID: 9881314.

paper.journal: Journal of the Royal College of Physicians of London
paper.citation: Brocklehurst J, Dickinson E, Windsor J. Sequential audits of geriatric care: measuring change in structure and process and the contribution of clinical audit. J R Coll Physicians Lond. 1998;32(6):564-567. doi:10.1016/s0035-8819(25)01805-7. PMID: 9881314.
paper.title: Sequential audits of geriatric care: measuring change in structure and process and the contribution of clinical audit.

title: A re-audit of pulmonary function laboratories in the West Midlands.
change: Recommendations to improve consistency and national and regional training workshops for laboratory staff.

detail.setting: 22 pulmonary function laboratories in the West Midlands
detail.intervention: Recommendations to improve consistency and national and regional training workshops for laboratory staff.

cycle2.result: Most variables had a coefficient of variation under 5%; improvements for predicted FEV1, TLC, TLCO, FVC, FRC and RV and measured FEV1 and FVC.

detail.other_findings: Predicted values from hypothetical subjects still varied unacceptably due to computer algorithm inconsistency; variation increased for predicted KCO and actual RV.
detail.citation: Dowson LJ, Mushtaq M, Watts T, Shurvinton J, Gooch R, Hayton R, et al.. A re-audit of pulmonary function laboratories in the West Midlands. Respir Med. 1998;92(9):1155-1162. doi:10.1016/s0954-6111(98)90411-5. PMID: 9926172.

paper.citation: Dowson LJ, Mushtaq M, Watts T, Shurvinton J, Gooch R, Hayton R, et al.. A re-audit of pulmonary function laboratories in the West Midlands. Respir Med. 1998;92(9):1155-1162. doi:10.1016/s0954-6111(98)90411-5. PMID: 9926172.
paper.title: A re-audit of pulmonary function laboratories in the West Midlands.

title: A repeated criterion-based audit of radiographic usage by a paediatric dentistry unit.
standard: Agreed good-practice criteria for radiographic usage (pre-planned checklist)
finding: Clinical note-keeping to accompany radiographic examinations was the least satisfactory area of practice.
change: Areas for improvement identified in the initial audit were addressed before re-audit.

detail.setting: Unit of Paediatric Dentistry, University Dental Hospital of Manchester

cycle1.result: Clinical note-keeping to accompany radiographic examinations was the least satisfactory area of practice.

detail.intervention: Areas for improvement identified in the initial audit were addressed before re-audit.
detail.other_findings: Criterion-based audit run through six 1-hour audit group meetings of unit staff and postgraduate students.
detail.citation: Shockledge RR, Hill FJ. A repeated criterion-based audit of radiographic usage by a paediatric dentistry unit. Int J Paediatr Dent. 1998;8(4):269-272. doi:10.1046/j.1365-263x.1998.00083.x. PMID: 9927928.

paper.citation: Shockledge RR, Hill FJ. A repeated criterion-based audit of radiographic usage by a paediatric dentistry unit. Int J Paediatr Dent. 1998;8(4):269-272. doi:10.1046/j.1365-263x.1998.00083.x. PMID: 9927928.
paper.title: A repeated criterion-based audit of radiographic usage by a paediatric dentistry unit.
